verdict.rationale: RustDesk documents running your own rendezvous/relay server, ships a Docker compose file for the OSS server, and says clients fall back to your relay when P2P fails. Hands-on users confirm years of use with their own lookup/relay server and a working Docker self-host. Some users found self-hosting hard or laggy, but none show it fails to work. Missing for 10: in-depth first-party self-hosting docs beyond the compose download step, authentication on the OSS self-hosted server (users report it is open without Pro), and encryption enabled by default.

support.subject: As an IT admin, I can self-host the rendezvous or relay infrastructure so session traffic stays on infrastructure I run

citations.quote: You can use our rendezvous/relay server, set up your own, or write your own rendezvous/relay server.
clients connect peer to peer when they can and fall back to your relay.
